extracted.intended_audience: early-career biomedical investigators (assistant professors) and institutional nominating officials
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and evaluation criteria for nomination and selection of Pew Biomedical Scholars — a four-year, $300,000 award for outstanding early-career biomedical investigators. Covers eligibility, selection priorities, award terms, reporting, and institutional nomination rules for the 2027 award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctorate requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Hold a doctorate in biomedical sciences, medicine, or a related field, including engineering or the physical sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment rank and independent lab (as of Sept. 3, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: As of Sept. 3, 2026, run an independent lab and hold a full-time appointment at the rank of assistant professor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointments such as research assistant professor, adjunct assistant professor, assistant professor research track, visiting professor, or instructor are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible appointment types (explicit exclusions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Current appointments such as research assistant professor, adjunct assistant professor, assistant professor research track, visiting professor, or instructor are not eligible to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-year appointment limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Must not have been appointed as an assistant professor and run an independent lab at any institution prior to June 10, 2023.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time spent in clinical internships, residencies, in work toward board certification, or on parental leave does not count as part of this three-year limit. Candidates who need an exception on the three-year limit should contact Pew’s program office to ensure that application reviewers are aware an exception has been given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application and nomination limits
rubrics_metrics.description: May apply to the program a maximum of two times. All applicants must be nominated by their institution and must complete the 2027 online application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicants have appointments at more than one eligible nominating institution or affiliate, they may not reapply in a subsequent year from a different nominating entity. May not be nominated for the Pew Scholars Program and the Pew-Stewart Scholars Program for Cancer Research in the same year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of research and exclusions (research type)
rubrics_metrics.description: Program supports science relevant to the advancement of human health; this program does not fund clinical trials research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong proposals will incorporate particularly creative and pioneering approaches to basic, translational, and applied biomedical research. Candidates whose work is based on biomedical principles but who bring in concepts and theories from more diverse fields are encouraged to apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of outstanding promise
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on their performance during their education and training, candidates should demonstrate outstanding promise as contributors in science relevant to human health.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-impact and innovative ideas encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas with the potential to produce an unusually high impact are encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria — project and researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of the successful candidates will be based on a detailed description of the work that the applicant proposes to undertake, evaluations of the candidate’s performance, and notable past accomplishments, including honors, awards, and publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In evaluating the candidates, the National Advisory Committee gives considerable weight to both the project proposal and the researcher, including evidence that the candidate is a successful independent investigator and has the skill set needed to carry out their high-impact proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of funding policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding from the NIH, other government sources, and project grants from nonprofit associations do not pose a conflict with the Pew scholars program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have questions concerning eligibility, please contact Pew Biomedical Programs in advance of applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: An award of $75,000 per year for four years will be provided to the sponsoring institution for use by the scholar, subject to annual review of the scholar’s progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant agreements will be issued in August of the award year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable uses of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The awarded funds may be used at the discretion of the Pew scholar, for personnel, equipment, supplies, or travel directly related to the scholar's research and as to best advance his or her research and career.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal investigator salary limit
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of the award that may be used for the principal investigator’s salary is limited to $12,500 per year (including benefits) or $50,000 over the duration of the grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no limits on student or postdoctoral salaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect costs (F&A) cap
rubrics_metrics.description: Not more than 8 percent ($24,000) of the total award value may be allocated for facilities and administration (F&A) charges or indirect costs (IDCs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover and no-cost extension policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the funds not be immediately required, they may be accumulated and carried over through the grant period and, with written approval of the program office, the grant may receive a no-cost extension for one additional year (without additional funds).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawards allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Subawards are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator effort expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is expected that Pew scholars will spend at least 80 percent of their time in work or activities related to the accomplishment of their overall research goals (which are not restricted to the specific aims proposed for this award).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, Pew provides flexible support to the general research aims of the scholar and does not require effort reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual meeting attendance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: During the four-year grant term, program participants are required to attend an annual meeting held in March or April.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All eligible expenses for attendees’ travel, lodging, and meals are paid by Pew. The meeting provides an opportunity to present research and for scientific collaboration and exchange with other scholars and members of the National Advisory Committee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual progress and financial reporting (funding contingency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual progress reports are required, describing research accomplishments, presentations, publications, project status, and future directions. In addition, financial reports are required annually accounting for general grant expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funding for the second, third, and fourth years is contingent upon timely submission of acceptable financial and narrative progress reports and attendance at the annual meeting during the four-year term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional nomination pool (participating institutions)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the awards to be made in 2027, one nomination will be invited from each of the listed institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Pew Charitable Trusts selects participating institutions based on the scope of the institution’s work in biomedical research and recommendations by the National Advisory Committee. Institutions that would like to be considered for invitation may contact the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review and selection body
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Advisory Committee provides scientific leadership to the program, reviews all applications, and identifies candidates to be recommended to Pew’s board to be named scholars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The committee's composition and stature (named members and affiliations) are provided to indicate the nature of peer review and selection.
